misconceptions.description: Believing vendor terms of service can supersede FERPA obligations
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts a vendor TOS as the operative privacy standard for student records
misconceptions.feedback: FERPA obligations attach to the institution and to vendors operating as school officials. Vendor-side terms cannot lower the floor; the institution's exposure governs.

misconceptions.description: Treating FERPA compliance as covering all educational AI ethics concerns
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites FERPA compliance as proof of ethical use
misconceptions.feedback: FERPA is one framework. IDEA imposes procedural due process for special-education-adjacent decisions; COPPA covers under-13 commercial collection; broader ethics concerns (surveillance, equity, persuasion, teacher authority) extend beyond all three.

misconceptions.description: Treating tool average accuracy as evidence of equitable deployment
misconceptions.trigger: learner answers 'is this tool equitable?' by reporting overall accuracy
misconceptions.feedback: Equity is about who has access and how distribution of benefits and harms varies across schools and learners. Average accuracy says nothing about distribution.

misconceptions.description: Believing COPPA covers all learners under 18
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites COPPA protections for adolescent users without checking age
misconceptions.feedback: COPPA strictly applies under 13. Ages 13-18 are a regulatory gap where designers should still apply ethical caution informed by developmental vulnerability, even though COPPA itself does not require it.
